title: ScaleIQ
shortDescription: A modern SaaS landing page built in React 19 + TypeScript for a platform that helps businesses collect more Google reviews using smart QR Codes and AI-powered review suggestions — featuring a custom CSS design system and TypeScript-first architecture.
overview: ScaleIQ is a SaaS product landing page built for a platform that helps businesses effortlessly collect more Google reviews through smart QR Codes and AI-powered review suggestion prompts. Built with React 19, Vite, and TypeScript, the project demonstrates a production-quality frontend architecture — with a custom CSS design system, colocated component styles, TypeScript interfaces, custom hooks, and a modular routing setup. The design is clean, conversion-focused, and professional — featuring a home page, features overview, pricing page, blog, auth pages, and account creation flow. The project uses Oxlint for modern, fast linting instead of traditional ESLint.
features: SaaS landing page with complete product marketing copy
Features page showcasing QR Code and AI review suggestion capabilities
Tiered pricing page with plan comparison
Blog section with SEO-optimized article listings
Authentication pages — Login and Create Account flows
Custom CSS design system with global design tokens
Colocated CSS files per component for scoped styling
Custom React hooks for scroll handling and UI behavior
TypeScript interfaces for all data structures and props
AuthLayout and MainLayout wrapper components for consistent page structure
React Router DOM routing with clean route configuration
Global animations and keyframes in centralized animation styles
Reusable UI component library — Buttons, Inputs, Accordions, etc.
Oxlint for fast, modern JavaScript/TypeScript linting
Fully responsive across all device sizes

architecture.description: Single Page Application built with React 19 and TypeScript. The project uses a clear separation of concerns — layout components, UI components, pages, hooks, constants, data, types, styles, and routes each have dedicated directories. CSS is colocated with components rather than centralized.

directoryStructure.components: High-level layout (Navbar, Footer) and reusable UI (Buttons, Inputs, Accordions)
directoryStructure.data: Static data and mock data used across pages
directoryStructure.pages: Application views (Home, Features, Pricing, Blog, Login, CreateAccount)
directoryStructure.styles: Global CSS, variables, animations, and typography

myRole: Sole Developer. Built the entire frontend architecture from scratch — including the TypeScript setup, CSS design system, component library, routing configuration, and all page content. Made architectural decisions for project structure, linting strategy, and state management patterns.
challenges: Setting up a TypeScript-first React project with proper type safety across components, hooks, and data layers without adding unnecessary complexity
Building a colocated CSS architecture where each component owns its own stylesheet — maintaining style encapsulation without a CSS-in-JS library
Designing a conversion-focused SaaS landing page that feels premium and professional while being built entirely with Vanilla CSS (no Tailwind or UI frameworks)
Configuring Oxlint as a replacement for ESLint — a newer, faster linter with different rule configurations
Creating a consistent design token system in CSS that scales across multiple pages and layout types
solutions: Used TypeScript interfaces in the dedicated types/ directory to define props, data structures, and hook return types, with strict mode enabled for maximum type safety
Structured the CSS architecture so each component file has a colocated .css file imported directly into the component — keeping styles scoped and easy to find during maintenance
Built a custom CSS design system in styles/variables.css with all design tokens (colors, spacing, typography, shadows) and referenced them throughout component stylesheets via CSS custom properties
Configured Oxlint in the project with React-specific rules for hooks and JSX, leveraging its Rust-based speed advantage for fast CI/CD linting

Defined all global animations in styles/animations.css as named @keyframes, then referenced animation names in component-level CSS — keeping animation logic centralized while application remains distributed
keyLearnings: TypeScript-first React architecture — proper interface design, generic types for reusable components, and strict mode configuration
Colocated CSS architecture as an alternative to CSS modules or CSS-in-JS for component-level style encapsulation
Oxlint configuration and its advantages over ESLint for React TypeScript projects
SaaS product marketing UI/UX — conversion-focused page design, pricing table patterns, and feature highlight structures
Building scalable CSS design token systems with custom properties across multi-page applications
